messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: kernel driver reset pattern (Xid 13/Xid 31) observed on infra-us-east-1 GPU hosts. Alerting on increased driver resets and pod restarts. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-driver-reset

Alex B: I'm on it. Which hosts are flapping?

Priya S: node-ius-12 and node-ius-14 showing recurring nv-host-reset messages. Telemetry shows ECC/correctable errors trending up before resets.

Marta R: Confirmed. Logs from node-ius-12 show repeated Xid=31 in dmesg then docker/containerd OOM/killing followed by driver reloads. Samples below:

```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65): 31, PID=0, GPU=0a
[ 1234.568001] containerd[2890]: panic: runtime: out of memory
[ 1234.568010] kernel: nv-hostreset: resetting GPU
```

Simon K: Impact matrix — small percentage (0.6%) of hosted-inference requests returned 502s in the last 10m, tail latency spiked 2x for a few customers. Not widespread but customer A and B may see degradation.

Jamie L: I've opened a customer bridge for the affected accounts and flagged for CS. Bridge link: https://zoom.redwood/bridge/4625

Chao W: Let's follow isolate -> cordon -> drain pattern. Plan: cordon the two flapping nodes, drain non-critical pods, move critical inference pods to dedicated hosts (redwood-dedicated pool) and throttle batch workloads.

Alex B: Steps I'm running now:

1) kubectl cordon node-ius-12
2) kubectl drain node-ius-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30 --timeout=5m
3) move inference pods via deployment scale/affinity tweak

Priya S: I'm collecting nvml and driver dumps: running nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 1 and tailing /var/log/messages for the reset window. Also pulling /var/log/nvidia-installer.log.

ops-bot: Action taken: node-ius-12 cordoned by Alex B at 4625002520. Evacuation initiated.

Marta R: While draining, I see a container crashloop on model-worker-v2 that correlates with the host reset. Suggest increasing readinessProbe timeout on that deployment temporarily to reduce churn.

Alex B: Doing a quick driver relaunch on node-ius-14 (systemctl restart nvidia-driver) and capturing kernel logs. Will patch with known safe driver from drivers.s3 if node doesn't stabilize.

deploy-bot: Rolling back driver package attempted on node-ius-14: package nv-driver-520.61 -> nv-driver-515.48. Action queued.

Priya S: Observed repeated ECC corrected counts rising ~120s before Xid bursts. Suspect hardware starting to fail; running memtest on that GPU and creating a hardware ticket with infra.

Simon K: For customer impact: routing policy enabled to fallback to model-variant-small for affected requests and to route non-critical requests to other regions. That reduced 502s. Updating status page in 5.

Jamie L: Status update to customers posted: "We are investigating intermittent GPU driver resets impacting a subset of inference requests in us-east-1. We're isolating affected hosts and shifting traffic. No data loss reported." :thumbsup:

Chao W: If driver restart doesn't hold, we'll quarantene the host from scheduler via label: kubectl label node node-ius-14 redwood/quarantine=true and add quota to capacity pool. Save logs: /var/crash/nv-*.tgz.

Alex B: Driver restart on node-ius-14 lasted ~7 minutes then reset again. Dumped nvenc and nvlink logs, uploading to /mnt/s3/incidents/4625002468/nv-dumps.tar.gz

Marta R: Can we enable continuous KV cache limits for model-worker to reduce memory pressure while we triage? Suggest config change: 

```
RUNTIME_BATCHER_MAX_TOKENS=2048
KV_CACHE_MAX_MB=512
```

This may reduce memory footprint and avoid triggering OOMs on flapping hosts.

Priya S: Collected driver debug output:

```
$ sudo dmesg | grep -i "NVRM: Xid"
[ 22345.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65): 13, PID=0, GPU=01, Thu Mar 11 12:34:56 2026
[ 22346.654321] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65): 31, PID=0, GPU=01
```

Attaching core logs to ticket RED-INF-4625.

Simon K: Ops recommendation: create a transient placement policy to avoid placing latency-sensitive inference on hosts with redwood/quarantine=true. Also add an automated eviction threshold: if node driver resets >3 in 10m, auto-quarantine.

Alex B: I'm provisioning replacement host in us-east-1 to take warmed containers while we mark the flappers for hardware diag. Bootstrapping new host now.

ops-bot: Auto-mitigation applied: routing fallback enabled for affected routes, batch job eviction triggered on nodes with >2 resets.

Jamie L: I've updated the status page: "Mitigations: traffic rerouted, hosts isolated, driver rollback in progress. Next update in 30m or upon customer impact change." 

Priya S: Next steps for postmortem checklist: capture node telemetry (nvidia-smi -q -x), list of pods impacted, kernel driver version history, and hardware health ticket with vendor. Also confirm if ECC correctable errors map to known hardware SKU.

Marta R: Will follow up with a temporary runtime config change to lower batch sizes for 1h and monitor. Setting alert thresholds: Xid spikes > 5/min should page oncall.

Alex B: Update: node-ius-12 stabilized after driver rollback to 515.48, no resets for 12m. node-ius-14 still flapping and has been quarantined. Bringing up replacement host and migrating workloads.

Simon K: Customer impact closed for now; degraded requests for a handful of customers resolved by routing and replacement host. We'll leave the incident open for postmortem and hardware follow-up.

Jamie L: Thanks team — I'll schedule the oncall handoff for next shift and assign owners for postmortem artifacts (Alex B driver trace, Priya S telemetry, Marta R runtime config). :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident 4625002468 status: MONITORED. Severity: SEV2. Owners assigned: Alex B, Priya S, Marta R.

Alex B: Logging final note: preserved crash dumps, quarantined failing GPU host, rolled back driver on one host, replacement provisioned. Postmortem will include timeline and proposed auto-quarantine rule.

Priya S: Adding note: open hardware vendor ticket and request RMA for GPU on node-ius-14. I have the serials and error counts attached.

Marta R: I'll push a short eval-run against core prompts to ensure no regression from reduced batch settings. Monitoring for 1h.

Simon K: Closing operational actions here. Will convert to postmortem in ~24h with data. Thanks everyone.
